item.title: Jameis Winston: Being a starting quarterback is what I dream of
item.description: The Giants are looking at their options for adding a quarterback in the wake of Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee injury, but it's Jameis Winston's show for now.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants are looking at their options for adding a quarterback in the wake of Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee injury, but it's Jameis Winston's show for now.

Winston replaced Dart when he was injured in Monday night's loss to the Rams and he's set to start against the Titans in Week 3. It's not Winston's first time in the role and he started two games when Dart was injured in 2025, but he called the prospect of getting almost an entire season in the role for the first time since leaving the Bucs after the 2019 season "a beautiful opportunity" to show what he's capable of doing.

"This is what I've always dreamed of, to be a starting quarterback," Winston said, via a transcript from the team. "Obviously, my respects and gratitude is just going to be with Jaxson, but at the same time, this is what I dream of. I dream of being what I am right now and executing at a high level."

Winston did not play well against the Rams, but said he is "very confident in my ability to execute with precision" in the weeks to come. With games against the Titans, Cardinals and Commanders in the next three weeks, the Giants will need that to happen immediately or their hopes of doing more than simply surviving the season won't be in great shape.

item.title: NFL news, live updates: Jaxson Dart to undergo season-ending knee surgery; Colts' Alec Pierce placed on IR
item.description: Follow along with the latest NFL news coming out of Week 2.
item.content:encoded:
Our second NFL week of the year is in the books, but unfortunately, it yielded a number of significant injuries, especially at the all-important quarterback position.

Unfortunately, injuries continued to dominate the headlines, with Giants QB Jaxson Dart exiting the game with a reported sprained MCL. He is reportedly set to undergo season-ending knee surgery after a promising start to his second NFL season. Jameis Winston is the team's backup. Wide receiver Malik Nabers also had an injury scare Monday night after his shoulder "popped out," but he returned to the field and said he was OK.

One day earlier, Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was carted off with a hamstring injury. The team received some positive news that Williams avoided a serious injury but was dubbed "week-to-week" by head coach Ben Johnson on Monday.

Also on Sunday, Washington Commanders star Jayden Daniels suffered a dislocated elbow — his second since last season. He is expected to miss time.

One team that is getting past a bad injury is the Falcons. After two weeks of disappointing outings from Cooper Rush, Atlanta announced on Monday that Michael Penix Jr. will start for the Falcons on Thursday against the Packers.

item.title: Panthers vs. Browns: Storylines to watch
item.description: Breaking down all the things to watch in this week’s game
item.content:encoded:
The Carolina Panthers are coming off their first win of the season, over the division rival Falcons. Their opponent this week is also coming off a win over an NFC South division rival, as the Browns defeated the Buccaneers 23-19. This put both teams’ 2026 seasons back on track at 1-1, and the Panthers will now visit the Browns in Cleveland on Sunday. The Panthers are riding high off a strong offensive start to the season for QB Bryce Young, and that’s my first storyline to keep track of.

Offense: Continue attacking down the field

The most surprising storyline coming out of two weeks of the NFL season across the league is the Panthers’ crazy effectiveness with the deep ball. Jalen Coker is rated the highest at deep ball effectiveness at WR by Pro Football Focus so far, and Tetairoa McMillan has also been an effective down field weapon for the team. Combine that with an insane air yard throw from Bryce to Xavier Legette this past Sunday, and its clear this Panthers team is pushing to be aggressive in the passing game. The Browns defense as a whole hasn’t been the best so far, but on paper they quietly have a very solid defense. They have a very solid secondary and a front seven that could cause problems for the Panthers rushing attack. The Panthers need to see the continued momentum from Bryce Young attacking down the field with touch and confidence, as he’s put together some of his best consecutive deep passing games in his career. I would expect offensive coordinator Brad Idzik to continue to be aggressive on that front.

Defense: Don’t sleep on Quinshon Judkins

The Browns faced two very good rushing defenses against the Jaguars and Buccaneers in consecutive weeks, and those teams held down the Browns rushing attack for the most part. Judkins only averaged 2.8 yards per carry in week 1 and 1.8 yards per carry in week 2, both pretty miserable performances for the former 2nd round pick who likely would have been picked in the 1st had he not had some off field issues. This could be a bounce back game for Judkins if the Browns focus on the rushing attack to try and stabilize the offense for QB Deshaun Watson, who himself had a decent bounce back performance last week against the Browns.

X Factor: Cleveland Browns young receiving core

The Browns spent high picks on WRs KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston in 2026, and drafted promising young TE Harold Fannin in 2025. Any time you have a receiving group that unproven, teams tend to view it as a weakness. However, Denzel Boston has caught 7 receptions for 154 yards and 2 TDs this season, Fannin has 7 catches for 75 yards, and Concepcion has 10 catches for 71 yards in two games. This is with Deshaun Watson at QB who hasn’t really played football for several years now. I wouldn’t underestimate these guys, even if the Panthers secondary matches up extremely well against them in theory. The Bears lit up this defense in the passing game week 1, admittedly with an all-world performance from their QB Caleb Williams. Still, I wouldn’t be surprised if many of these guys eat well on Sunday and the game is much closer than many fans expect.

What storylines are you watching this weekend, Panthers fans?

item.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba wins award that will help a local Seattle charity
item.description: JSN’s Week 2 dominance was nationally recognized, and will help to serve a good cause.
item.content:encoded:
While quarterbacks are usually the ones that get talked about first on morning shows, and we see them first in the box scores, it is a wideout for the Seattle Seahawks that has served as the engine for the offense so far in 2026.

After a 155-yard, 3 TD performance against the Arizona Cardinals, the reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year has won the FedEx Air & Ground NFL Player of the Week award. Unlike the NFL’s Player of the Week awards, the FedEx Air & Ground is won via fan vote.

Despite his young career, Smith-Njigba is already writing his name in the Seattle record books. This past Sunday’s display of brilliance broke a tie with Steve Largent, Brian Blades and Tyler Lockett for the most games of 150+ receiving yards and 2+ receiving TD’s (3) from any Seahawks receiver ever.

Check out this tweet, for a quick breakdown of his immediate 82-yard reception (a career long) for a house call, as well as the rest of his hat-trick game in ‘Zona.

According to the NFL’s website, “FedEx will make a $2,000 donation to Feeding America in honor of each player.” Smith-Njigba has catalyzed that donation to be sent to Seattle’s, Food Lifeline to address local level food insecurity.

Josh Allen, of the Buffalo Bills, joins JSN as the winner of the Air and Ground NFL Player of the Week.

item.title: Broncos vs. Rams: 3 Things to Watch for in Week 3
item.description: The Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football. Here are three storylines to keep your eyes on.
item.content:encoded:
Coming off an impressive comeback victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Denver Broncos earned a much-needed confidence boost heading into their matchup versus the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football. Here are three storylines for Broncos Country to keep a close eye on in Denver’s Week 3 primetime game hosting the Rams.

Will Jaylen Waddle have another impact game and shine in primetime?

One of the highlights in their victory over the Jaguars was how dominant wide receiver Jaylen Waddle was. After being virtually shut down in Week 1 against the Kansas City Chiefs, Waddle had a tremendous impact last Sunday and was the highlight player for the Broncos offensively.

He reeled in eight receptions on ten targets for 138 yards. Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb did a great job utilizing Waddle in a variety of manners from the slot to ‘Z’. I felt Webb was fantastic isolating him in mismatch scenarios against a tough Jaguars defense.

How the Broncos choose to deploy Waddle on a weekly basis will certainly be one of the most intriguing aspects of the season. The Rams spent a lot of money this offseason revamping their secondary via free agency additions or making big trades. It’ll be interesting to see how Denver comes up with a gameplan to attack that. For the second straight week, my money is on Waddle playing a big role for the Broncos’ offense.

Can Bo Nix pick up where he left off against the Jaguars?

Head Coach Sean Payton called the Broncos’ affair against the Jaguars a tale of two halves. The offense struggled in the first quarter of the game. Through fifteen minutes of play, all three of their drives resulted in punts. Denver didn’t achieve a second down until the second quarter and only netted three points in two redzone trips before halftime.

In the second half, Nix seemed much more poised in the pocket. He put together another impressive fourth quarter rally which earned him yet another comeback victory. Webb’s half time adjustments played a big role in that. He helped set Nix up for success by getting him to throw on the move and having him get some more looks under center.

It will be important for Nix and the Broncos’ offense to start off hot and forego their slow starts. Nobody wants to see Denver have to try and rally back against a well-coached team that scored the most points in the NFL last season. I’m optimistic Nix can deliver, but the offensive line will have to give him a chance to make plays.

What’s the defensive plan to combat the Rams’ offense?

The Rams had an uncharacteristically bad game in their season opener against the San Francisco 49ers. Though they looked much better and reverted to top form against the New York Giants on Monday Night Football.

Stafford threw for over 300 yards and had four touchdowns. Keep in mind, that was without Puka Nacua—whose availability for Sunday Night Football is still up in the air. With Nacua out, Davante Adams went off and hauled in eight catches for 195 yards and 2 touchdowns. Even with Denver’s talented secondary, Adams could prove to be a problem depending on who is tasked with covering him.

Additionally, their running back duo of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combined for 164 yards rushing on just 24 carries. In addition to those players, the Rams also have a handful of intriguing players at tight end. Terrance Ferguson is an emerging player in their offense and looked good last week.

Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph is going to have his hands full again this week coming up with another game plan to stop a talented and high-scoring Sean McVay offense. Even so, Broncos Country should be optimistic they can do that, especially given how well the group performed against the Jaguars last Sunday.

item.title: Remembering a Random Packers Game: The Atlanta Falcons
item.description: Our journey back in time makes a stop in 2011 for the Green Bay Packers and the Atlanta Falcons.
item.content:encoded:
Each week this season, I’ve been taking a trip back in time to look at a game between the Green Bay Packers and their opponent during that given week. A random number generator has been deciding which game I cover. So far, I’ve covered a 1999 win against the Vikings and a 1981 loss to the Jets. This week: let’s look at the Atlanta Falcons, whom the Packers have played 36 total times.

I want to preface this by saying I PROMISE that this number was random. We’re going to look at the 28th overall matchup between the two teams, which happens to be one of my favorite football games of all time: the 2010 NFC Divisional Playoff game, which took place on January 15th, 2011. I could talk about this game all day, but I’ll try to keep it as concise as possible.

Entering the Game

After a heartbreaking end to the 2009 season which saw them lose what is still the highest-scoring playoff game in NFL history, the 2010 Green Bay Packers had been put through the wringer. Week after week, another player suffered a season-ending injury. They lost RB Ryan Grant, DE Justin Harrell, LB Nick Barnett, TE Jermichael Finley, S Morgan Burnett, RT Mark Tauscher, LB Brady Poppinga, LB Brad Jones, DE Mike Neal, LB Brandon Chillar, TE Spencer Havner, S Derrick Martin, S Anthony Smith…who else?

Oh! Rising star QB Aaron Rodgers missed a game with a concussion (his second of the year!), while the team was in the middle of a high stakes battle for the playoffs. LB Clay Matthews missed a game while battling a lingering hamstring injury. Always-reliable WR Donald Driver missed a game due to injury for the first time since the 2003 season. DE Cullen Jenkins missed a number of games with a calf injury. I mean, the Packers quite literally limped into the playoffs as the #6 seed with a 10-6 record.

And then…they won their first playoff game, the Wild Card matchup against the #3 seed Philadelphia Eagles (another game I could talk about for days). Suddenly, we were feeling a little powerful. There was a big, BIG game coming up next, however: the 13-3 #1 seed Atlanta Falcons, who had beaten the Packers earlier that season, 20-17. Their biggest test yet.

Key Moments

Things got off to a horrible start for the offense. After the Packers forced a punt on the Falcons’ first drive, RB James Starks lost 3 yards on 1st and 10. Aaron Rodgers then threw an incompletion. And on 3rd and 10: a 30 yard completion to Greg Jennings…who fumbled.

Already in Packers territory, the Falcons scored, eating up almost 4 minutes of clock in the process. The Packers needed to answer, and they did, with a drive which ended in a 6 yard Jordy Nelson TD. All tied up, 7-7.

The ensuing kickoff by Mason Crosby was promptly returned 102 yards by Eric Weems for a TD. This was, at the time, the longest play in NFL playoff history. For the Packers and their fans watching the game, it was a crushing blow. Falcons 14, Packers 7.

The Packers then…scored again to tie things at 14? I’m sorry, do we have a shootout on our hands? Answer: no! The Falcons got the ball back with 6 minutes left in the first half, and were hopeful of going into halftime with a lead. Instead, Matt Ryan went on to throw an endzone interception to Tramon Williams, who was putting together a nice little playoff highlight reel. We then witnessed an Aaron Rodgers masterclass, as he got the Packers back into the endzone in under 2 minutes. Packers 21, Falcons 14.

But wait! There’s more!

With 37 seconds left in the first half, the Falcons tried their best to get downfield. With the Packers set to have the first possession after halftime, even a field goal would’ve been helpful. They were almost there, but there was enough time left for another play before they attempted to kick. One might even say “they tried to bite off more yardage and…”, well, you know what happened next.

Suddenly, it was halftime, and the game had completely turned on its head. The Packers were up 28-14, and got the ball back to start the second half. What do you know, they scored again! Packers 35, Falcons 14.

After a quick three and out by the Falcons, the Packers got the ball back and, you guessed it: scored again. After being down 14-7, the Packers scored 35 unanswered points, and were up 42-14. The Falcons would go on to score just once more during the remainder of the game, while Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers ate up the remainder of the game clock, adding 6 more points in the process.

The Outcome

When the clock hit 00:00, the Packers found themselves heading to the NFC Championship for the first time in 3 years after taking down the juggernaut Atlanta Falcons, 48-21. Aaron Rodgers gave us one of the greatest games we’ve ever seen from him, completing 31 of 36 passes for 366 yards, 3 TDs and 0 INTs. James Starks led the team on the ground, rushing 25 times for 66 yards. 4 different receivers had at least 75 yards: James Jones (75), Donald Driver (76), Jordy Nelson (79), and Greg Jennings (101). Tramon Williams finished the night with 2 INTs and 1 TD. Clay Matthews (2), Charles Woodson (1), C.J. Wilson (1), and B.J. Raji (1) all recorded at least one sack.

The Packers would go on to beat the division rival Chicago Bears in the NFC Championship, 21-14, and they traveled back to the Super Bowl for the first time since the 1997 season. Then, and it never gets old saying this, the Green Bay Packers won Super Bowl XLV after defeating the Pittsburgh Steelers, 31-25. Pure bliss.

The 1-1 Packers play their 2026 home opener on Thursday Night Football against the 0-2 Atlanta Falconsat 7:15 PM local time.

item.title: Tony Dungy says he's 'not bitter' about losing Hall of Fame vote | Exclusive
item.description: Former NFL player, coach and broadcaster Tony Dungy was among 27 people recently removed from the Pro Football Hall of Fame's selection committee.
item.content:encoded:
Tony Dungy is not bitter, angry, upset, frustrated, bewildered or mad. The Hall of Fame coach is instead taking it in stride that he is among 27 people recently removed from the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s selection committee as part of sweeping changes.

“I served my time on the committee, I was glad to do it,” Dungy told USA TODAY Sports this week. "It was something that was important to me. I don’t mind not being on the committee. I know they’ve made decisions on how they want to do things and that’s fine.

“My suggestion to them would be to examine the process and don’t have three-, four- and five-person classes going forward, when we have more candidates in the mix. It doesn’t make sense to put less people in.”

Dungy, 70, the first Black coach to win a Super Bowl and an inductee from the Hall’s Class of 2016, was arguably the most prominent member leaving the selection committee. He served six years as a voter. Hall of Fame receiver James Lofton has also left after 10 years on the committee, resigning before any decisions were made regarding his status. And Hall of Fame general manager Bill Polian, who teamed with Dungy with the Indianapolis Colts, is also out after six years as a voter.

Four media members who served 30-plus years as selectors – Frank Cooney (33 years), John McClain (31), Tony Grossi (31) and Rick Gosselin (30) – were also removed. And Lisa Salters, the esteemed ESPN reporter, is done after six years on the committee.  

In addition to reducing the size of the selection committee from 50 to 25 (plus three additional non-voting selectors), the hall also eliminated the seniors category – placing all former players in a single pool – and streamlined the voting process.

Although the Hall received a torrent of criticism earlier this year when six-time Super Bowl-winning coach Bill Belichick wasn’t selected in his first year on the ballot – prompting Hall of Fame director Jim Porter to declare there would be an examination of the process – it is also true that officials contemplated changes before the Belichick omission.

Disclosure: I’ve been a member of the selection committee for 29 years.

In Dungy’s case, the Hall of Fame coach won’t publicly reveal how he voted for any of the candidates and was careful not to criticize the committee or hall administrators.

In other words, he doesn’t want to come off as sour grapes.

“I’m not bitter or upset or anything about not being on,” Dungy said. “They asked for my time on the committee, I did it, I enjoyed it. It wasn’t easy, but it was something I felt good about doing.”

item.title: This week's NFL officiating video reminded teams not to line up offside on the tush push
item.description: The NFL is reminding teams not to line up offside on the tush push.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL is reminding teams not to line up offside on the tush push.

In a video sent to all 32 teams this week, NFL officiating and rules analyst Walt Anderson used a Seahawks tush push, which was called for offensive offside, to illustrate the type of penalty that will be called.

"We have covered this before, but clubs are reminded on both sides of the ball to line up properly on these push plays," Anderson said.

Anderson showed how the Seahawks were aligned on the play, which was snapped to tight end AJ Barner for a first down but called back because of the penalty, and said one Seahawk had both his hand and helmet in the neutral zone, and another had his hand in the neutral zone.

"Here, this hand is clearly offside, this head is clearly offside, as is the right hand of the tight end," Anderson said.

During the unsuccessful attempt to ban the tush push in 2025, one of the arguments against it was that it was too hard to officiate. The league is still trying to make sure everyone understands exactly what will and will not be flagged.

item.title: Colts Week 2 Film Analysis: Painful Performance in Primetime
item.description: The Colts still have time to turn their season around, but are running out of time to fix their defense.
item.content:encoded:
The Indianapolis Colts are 0-2.

First and foremost, I’m not ready to write off the season just yet. But I also will do my best to avoid sugarcoating what we’ve seen so far.

For a team that is this desperate to get over the hump and sneak into the playoffs, it’s never encouraging when you give up 1000 yards to two QBs that you will certainly see in the playoffs. But what I think is quietly encouraging is that the offense had a bounce back game and put up 30 points in one of the most vaunted stages in the sport: Primetime in Arrowhead.

Let’s start with Daniel Jones because I thought outside of a brutal INT, he was tremendous.

The Chiefs do a great job of rotating safeties here to disguise a version of 2-man. Ring is a coverage in the Vic Fangio system that is a way to roll coverage to a dangerous receiver while playing 2 man. Essentially it’s man coverage across the board, but with a Cover 6 shell on top of it. You can see them roll their coverage toward Alec Pierce.

In 2-man, corners are going to play with heavy inside leverage, because that’s where the big play is waiting to happen. The corner here isn’t trying to disguise anything. Keenan is running an in-breaking route vs. heavy inside leverage. That route is dead unless you’re prime Davante Adams.

The Colts got to Tosser (two slants or double slants) to beat a lot of Spags third down pressure looks. It’s as simple as it gets on a chalkboard, but very difficult to execute. The golden rule of pass protection is to never let any free runners through the A and B gaps— and Spags gets it done all the time.

Daniel Jones had to throw around free runners in the throwing window all night and he did it. The ball placement isn’t going to be perfect, but completing it all that matters on third down.

This was the play I was most impressed with. When the Colts got the ball in OT, Jones uncorked a big post route to Laquon Treadwell and completely flipped the field. A lot of people have said this ball is underthrown, and while I will concede that it is, only slightly. It’s a great ball that doesn’t give the DB a chance to make a play on it.

I want to get to the defense but it’s only right that I talk about the end of the game here. I did not like the decision to run the ball at the end of the game, but the look is absolutelythere.

As for the 4th&8? I don’t hate the decision to kick it, though maybe I’m on an island on that. If they didn’t get the look they wanted, then why do it? I think it’s pretty delusional to assume that Treadwell or Keenan Allen were going to win a matchup on the outside with that down and distance. So would you rather lose the game there, or kick the FG and see what happens. I know it’s Mahomes. I know the defense was playing terrible. But if you go for it on 4th&8 you’re basically telling everyone on your defense you have zero faith in them. How is that supposed to help them ever turn this thing around? It never will.

The Colts get to a Non Traditional Tampa from a mugged up alignment. This post route from Thorton should never be available. Never! But since Cam Taylor-Britt did not get to his zone on the other half, it’s a massive play. If anything Thorton could have walked right in if it wasn’t for Carlies forcing Mahomes to layer this throw over the top.

The Colts are in Drop 8 coverage here vs. Empty. But nobody is aligned properly because nobody is outside leveraged on Walker. It’s an easy pitch and catch to setup a touchdown. This is bad defense!

BOTTOM LINE

The Colts still have time to turn their season around, but they are running out of time to fix their defense. The offense did their part after being punched in the mouth vs. Baltimore. The defense did not. 1000 yards in two weeks is simply unacceptable.

My biggest takeaway is that Shane Steichen coached his ass off, until the final sequence. Without Alec Pierce it’s very difficult to go blow-for-blow with Mahomes and Walker (especially when your defense is playing that poorly).

But how many games, and really seasons, in the NFL can you coach where you get outplayed in the 4th quarter?

We’ll see how the loss of Pierce ultimately affects this offense long term, but I do think the Colts are going to have to be more creative in the run game. Teams should rightfully sell out vs. the run, and until the Colts punish them for doing that, it’s going to be tough sledding.

Defensively, the pressure has to be at an all-time high. Under no circumstances can the Colts defense look that bad again. There’s never perfect comparison in the NFL, but in 2024 the Gus Bradley defense had a very rough start to the season, but even they eventually settled in during Week 3. I don’t think you can justify having an $100M secondary and look even worse than the defense that you eventually decided you had to replace.

item.title: Giants reportedly pursuing Jimmy Garoppolo after Jaxson Dart injury
item.description: Couuld there be mutual interest between the Giants and the veteran quarterback?
item.content:encoded:
The New York Giants appear to be taking a big swing in their efforts to fill the quarterback vacancy created by Jaxson Dart’s season-ending injury. There are reports that the Giants have interest in Jimmy Garoppolo, and there is a possibilty that interest could be reciprocated.

Among available practice squad and free-agent options the Giants would not have to trade for, going after Garoppolo is likely the biggest swing they could take. Unless they tried to talk Russell Wilson out of retirement, and that would seem highly unlikely, Garoppolo is the most accomplished quarterback on the market.

Jimmy G., 34, was a second-round pick by the New England Patriots in 2014. He has appeared in 85 regular-season games, and has a 43-21 record in 64 career starts across 12 seasons. Garoppolo quarterbacked the San Francisco 49ers to the Super Bowl in the 2019 season, where the 49ers lost to the Kansas City Chiefs.

Garoppolo spent the last two seasons backing up Matthew Stafford with the Los Angeles Rams. He played in three games last season, but did not throw a pass. In 2024, he played in just one game. In that game, he went 27 of 41 for 334 yards with two touchdown passes and an interception

Garoppolo elected free agency this past offseason. NFL Network insider Mike Garafolo believes the Giants are one of the few teams Garoppolo would be interested in playing for.

Jameis Winston, with a freshly-minted two-year, $13 million contract extension that ties him to the Giants through the 2028 season, will be the Giants’ starter in Dart’s absence. Jake Haener, currently on the practice squad, is the only other quarterback currently under contract to the Giants.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Wednesday that “all options are open” to supplement the quarterback position in Dart’s absence.

The Giants won’t be in a hurry to replace Winston. Trading for a quarterback at some point, though, is a possibility — especially if Winston is ineffective or gets injured. Considering the rash of injuries to quarterbacks over the first two weeks of the season, teams might be loathe to trade quarterback depth this early in the season.

So, the Giants want a veteran “been there and done that” option, Garoppolo might be their best bet right now.

item.title: Will Donovan Jennings start again at left guard?
item.description: Jennings or Jager Burton will need to be back in the lineup with Aaron Banks ruled out.
item.content:encoded:
If you thought that the Green Bay Packers’ week one offensive line questions were terrifying, just wait until tonight.

In that game, all the Packers really had to worry about was settling the left guard position with Aaron Banks out. On the eve of their week 3 matchup with the Atlanta Falcons, the Packers ruled Banks out once again, and now they’re also missing right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele for the season.

At least the backup right tackle decision is easy: that will be Anthony Belton. But deciding on who to put at left guard in Banks’ place is less clear. They could just go back to Donovan Jennings, who started in Week 1 and who was the first man off the bench when Banks was hurt against the Jets last Sunday. Then again, Jennings played awfully in the opener and got banged up himself in Week 2, leading to playing time for Jager Burton.

Burton wasn’t bad in his short stint, either! And he got into the fray to stick up for his quarterback when Jordan Love took a big hit going across the goal line. Will he get the start over Jennings? We probably won’t know until warmups, as OC Adam Stenavich wasn’t giving anything away on Wednesday.

While we fret over the line, at least the defense has found a star in the slot. Let’s look at Javon Bullard’s hot start to the season to give us some excitement heading into Thursday Night Football.

This Is How Javon Bullard Beat Physics, ‘Changed the Math’ for Packers | SI.com
Bullard has looked like a star through two games this season, and his play in the fourth quarter — standing up a 320-plus tackle and making a tackle for loss on Breece Hall — is just one example of the physicality he’s bringing in Jonathan Gannon’s defense. Bullard, for his part, says he thinks he’s “one of the baddest people alive.”

Packers S Javon Bullard ‘can find another gear’ | Packers.com
The Packers’ coordinators spoke on Wednesday and Jonathan Gannon thinks Bullard is one of the best nickels he has been around — high praise indeed. Meanwhile, here’s Adam Stenavich on what he hopes to see out of the guards competing to play with Aaron Banks out:

“Go out there, compete, be productive, be clean, eliminate penalties and just make it really hard on us to take you off the field if you’re one of those backup guys. That’s really what I want to see.”

Meet Cam Achord: The Packers’ secret special teams weapon | ESPN
It certainly seems that Green Bay’s special teams have improved from last year, and Achord is right in the middle of that improvement. This is perhaps the deepest dive into the team’s new coordinator, who once got a broken nose from Patriots special teams ace Justin Bethel.

Penalties, unsurprisingly, are one of them. Rushing yards and third down conversion rate are two others. A functional offensive line would certainly help!

item.title: This chart proves Titans OT JC Latham is better than you think
item.description: Tennessee Titans OT JC Latham is way better than the average fan thinks.
item.content:encoded:
Tennessee Titans offensive tackle JC Latham is a player who always seems to draw controversial opinions. Some Titans fans believe he’s growing into a franchise right tackle. Others claim he needs replacing ASAP, or needs to switch positions inside to guard.

Latham is arguably the Titans’ most polarizing player. In Sunday’s nailbiting Week 2 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, he gave up an ill-timed sack on a questionable bootleg play-call on 1st-and-goal late in the fourth quarter. Latham does have a tendency to make glaring mistakes, drawing criticism he doesn’t always deserve.

The honest account is that Latham is a very good, ascending blocker. His 1-2 mistakes per weekend tend to be glaring, with some Titans fans forming overreactionary takes.

A recent pass-blocking chart from Pro Football Focus highlights how good Latham has actually been for the Titans through two weeks. The former Alabama standout has the highest “island rate” of any offensive tackle in the NFL, meaning he’s faced more one-on-one matchups than any other OT. Despite that, Latham has won the fifth-most matchups of any tackle when left on an island.

This means the Titans trust Latham to win one-on-one matchups. The results indicate he’s repaying their faith by doing just that at a very effective clip. Latham is still a 23-year-old blocker on the third year of his rookie contract. He’s undeniably an above-average right tackle with room to get better.

PFF has credited Latham with allowing just three pressures and zero sacks this season, though he definitely deserved blame for that Jalen Carter sack. He’s faced some good pass rushers on the Jets and Eagles such as David Bailey, Jalyx Hunt, and Nolan Smith. Most of the time, Lahtam is providing Titans QB Cam Ward with clean pockets.

Titans fans need to confront the truth about Latham.

item.title: 5 Qs Lions vs. Jets preview: Big game from Amon-Ra St. Brown incoming?
item.description: Here’s our preview with Gang Green Nation about this Week 3 matchup between the Detroit Lions and New York Jets.
item.content:encoded:
Reunited and it feels… nostalgic.

This week, we had the pleasure of connecting with MacGregor Wells, the Deputy Manager for Gang Green Nation, to give us some insight into who these New York Jets are through two weeks. We learned how Jets fans are still very much in a “wait and see” moment with this football team, what Geno Smith needs to do in order to be successful during his second stint in Gotham, and what to make of these suffocating performances from the defense—and much more.

1. The New York Jets are off to about as good of a start as they could have anticipated. Led by Aaron Glenn, this defense ranks third in DVOA–first in run defense and sixth in pass defense. For all the mockery they faced at last year’s trade deadline, the Jets look like they’re a team on the rise.

But after losing last week to the Green Bay Packers, with the questions surrounding Glenn’s game-management decisions, does it still feel like it appears to be from the outside looking in at this team?

I think for the most part we’re in wait and see mode at this point in the season.The Jets defense has played well, but they have benefitted from the schedule, which started with a very bad Titans offense the Jets manhandled. Then we had a sloppy game in the rain against a Packers team with what looks like a bad offensive line dealing with multiple injuries. You can only play the teams on the schedule, and so far the Jets defense has done well, but I think the jury’s out on what this will look like against the better offenses in the NFL. The Jets secondary is of particular concern. I think over the course of the season we will see the Jets secondary get exploited.

On offense the Jets have a good offensive line and some pretty good weapons in Breece Hall and Garrett Wilson, but so far that side of the ball remains a work in progress. They did well against a bad Titans team but struggled against the Packers. Are the Jets on the rise? I suppose, but coming off one of the worst teams I have ever seen last year, on the rise is expected; it would be difficult to be worse. 

2. Geno Smith’s triumphant return to the team that drafted him 13 years ago is one helluva winding circle back to where it all started. Glenn moved on from Tanner Engstrand in January and hired veteran offensive mind Frank Reich to be the team’s third offensive coordinator in as many years. Smith’s lone season in Las Vegas was disastrous, finishing with a league-high 17 interceptions.

It’s interesting to see Smith completing over 70% of his passes, sixth in completion percentage over expected, and 16th in EPA/dropback. How has Geno gotten off to such a sound start, what role has Reich served in that turnaround, and how optimistic are you in Smith playing the kind of football he needs to play when the other side of the ball is playing the way they are?

Smith has always been an accurate quarterback with a strong arm. The issues with him haven’t been with his arm talent. The issues have always been his decision making and his ability to process what’s in front of him in a timely manner. He has always been prone to turnovers. While he has avoided turnovers thus far this year, I doubt he has changed this part of his game so late in his career. Ultimately if you don’t ask too much of Smith he can competently execute the offense. Give him enough time and he will deliver the ball accurately. The Jets have a pretty good offensive line so there should be a good number of games when Smith has plenty of time and he’ll competently execute the offense. However, there will be games when the offensive line allows pressure on Smith. Then he and the Jets offense will struggle. Sacks and turnovers will follow. Ask him to carry the team and Smith will likely implode.

3. New York’s stifling start on defense has a lot to do with their top draft pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, David Bailey. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, “Bailey has generated 11 pressures (23.4% pressure rate) and two sacks on 47 pass rushes, the third-most pressures by a rookie edge rusher through Week 2 in the Next Gen Stats era, trailing only Nick Bosa and Josh Hines-Allen (12 each in 2019).” His incredible athleticism is making all the difference right now, also according to Next Gen Stats: “Bailey is averaging a 0.75 second get-off time, the seventh-fastest among 92 edge rushers with at least 40 pass rushes. His 11 pressures are more than the rest of the Jets’ edge rushers combined (10).”

With numbers like this Bailey has to be popping off the screen. Where is he primarily lining up on defense, what sort of versatility has he shown, and did the Jets just get the steal of last year’s draft?

Bailey is primarily lining up on the edge. He is playing with his hand in the dirt at times and as a stand up pass rusher at other times. The Jets will occasionally drop him into coverage. I’m not sure that’s a great idea, other than as a rare gimmick to try to confuse the offense. Did the Jets get the steal of the draft? Oh, I don’t know. Two things here. First, I don’t think we can draw much in the way of conclusions based on two games. Second, Bailey was the #2 pick. At that slot it’s pretty difficult to be the steal of the draft. Great things are expected from #2 overall picks. To be the steal of the draft he’d have to outperform already sky high expectations. I like what I’ve seen for the most part from Bailey, but I would hesitate to already call him the steal of the draft.

4. The Jets’ defense has put up some incredibly eye-popping performances through two weeks. They held both the Titans and the Packers to less than 200 total yards in back-to-back weeks, and they’re tied for the fourth-best mark in EPA per play allowed (-0.25) and sack rate (8.5%).

Which players, outside of Bailey, have been key to New York’s impressive defensive play to start the season? Have you noticed any new wrinkles to the defense, or any new emphases placed on this side of the ball?

The Jets defense has played well so far, though, as discussed above, the schedule has probably had something to do with this. I would say the players who have stood out so far other than Bailey would be edge Kingsley Enagbare, who has surprised me with his stout overall play, defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat, who has done great work against the run, safety Dane Belton, who has been a sure tackler and fundamentally sound at his position, and second year cornerback Azareye’h Thomas, who has been sticky in coverage despite his speed limitations. The Jets are finding success by shutting down the run with strong defensive line play early, then putting pressure on the quarterback when he has to pass. This isn’t some revolutionary scheme, just sound fundamental defensive football so far. We’ll see how that holds up against better offenses. The secondary still appears to me to be vulnerable against better offenses. 

5. The Jets opened as 7.5-point underdogs heading into Week 3 against a Lions team still licking their wounds after taking a beating the entire world saw courtesy of Josh Allen and Co. Since then the line has moved to the Lions being a 6.5-point favorite over at FanDuel Sportsbook.

What’s one thing you want to see, what’s one thing you need to see, and one thing you’re sure you’ll see happen at Ford Field this Sunday?

One thing I want to see: the Jets getting first round pick Kenyon Sadiq more involved in the offense. They spent the 16th pick in the first round on a tight end. They need to get more production out of him. 

One thing I need to see: Breece Hall running more effectively. The Jets gave Hall a big bucks contract extension, presumably to be the bell cow back. Thus far this season his performance has been underwhelming to say the least. It’s just two games, but I need to see a lot more from Hall going forward.

One thing I’m sure I’ll see: Amon Ra St. Brown torching the Jets secondary. Let’s be real here, the Jets don’t have anyone who can stick with St. Brown. The only way this doesn’t happen is if Jared Goff is so harried by the Jets pass rush he has no time to get the ball to St. Brown. I don’t think that will happen.

item.title: Jaguars vs. Patriots: Matchup History Through the Decades
item.description: The Jaguars and Patriots have played each other 15 times, and the Patriots currently lead the series 12-3
item.content:encoded:
After a crushing loss on the road, the Jaguars are back in Jacksonville this week hosting the New England Patriots. The two teams have faced off against each other 15 times, and the Patriots currently lead the series 12-3. The Jags’ only wins have happened at home, so let’s revisit the Jags defeating the Patriots through the decades.

The 1990’s

AFC Wild Card on January 3, 1999
Final score: Patriots 10 – Jaguars 25
Attendance: 71,139

Jacksonville recorded 17 first downs, 308 total net yards, and 32 minutes of possession, while New England managed 14 first downs, 206 net yards, and a 28 minute time of possession. Fred Taylor and Jimmy Smith scored touchdowns. Mark Brunell completed 14 out of 34 attempted passes for 161 yards and was sacked twice for a loss of 13 yards. Fred Taylor led the team with 162 rushing yards, and Keenan McCardell led with 72 receiving yards. Mike Hollis made the four attempted field goals. Chris Hudson had a 17-yard interception. Tony Brackens and Joel Smeenge recorded sacks on Scott Zolak for a loss of 19 yards.

The 2000’s

They tried.

The 2010’s

Week 2 on September 16, 2018
Final score: Patriots 20 – Jaguars 31
Attendance: 68,527

We all know what happened during the previous meeting between the two teams. Donte Moncrief, Keelan Cole, Austin Seferian-Jenkins, and Dede Westbrook scored touchdowns. Blake Bortles completed 29 out of 45 attempted passes for 376 yards. T.J. Yeldon led the team with 58 rushing yards, and Cole led the team with 116 receiving yards. Josh Lambo made the attempted field goal. D.J. Hayden and Dante Fowler Jr. recorded sacks on Tom Brady for a loss of 14 yards. Telvin Smith and Myles Jack both registered eight total tackles.

The 2020’s

Week 7 on Oct 20, 2024
Final score: Patriots 16 – Jaguars 32
Attendance: 86,651

I understand that this game was played in London, but the Jags were the designated home team, so I’m counting it. The first quarter was highlighted by Devin Lloyd sacking Drake Maye, and Jamycal Hasty scored a touchdown for the Patriots during the first drive, marking the team’s first time doing so for the season. The Pats had the lead 10-0, and despite Cam Robinson being evaluated for a concussion, the offense started heating up. First, Gabe Davis got a first down, Christian Kirk picked up twenty yards, D’Ernest Johnson got a first down, followed by Tank Bigsby with a first down. Lawrence connected with Brian Thomas Jr. in the end zone to put seven on the board. Lawrence found BTJ again for a gain of 58, then Bigsby ran it in to give the Jaguars the lead. Eight minutes later, Parker Washington returns the punt for 96 yards, and Lawrence hits BTJ for the two-point conversion. Cam Little brings the score to 25-10 during the third quarter. The Patriots score at the top of the fourth, but Bigsby strikes back with another touchdown with 1:45 left in the game.

item.title: Denver Broncos look to continue success vs. NFC opponents
item.description: In the last nine games against NFC teams, the Broncos are 9-0. All streaks end. When will this one?
item.content:encoded:
The Denver Broncos look to continue its success against NFC opponents in Week 3 when they host the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football. In the last nine games against NFC teams, the Broncos are 9-0.

In fact, Bo Nix has only lost a single game against NFC teams and that was his first ever start in the league. That’s wild to think about. He is 9-1 all-time.

Bo Nix career vs. NFC

  • 2024, Week 1: Seattle Seahawks (20-26) L
  • 2024, Week 3: Tampa Bay Buccaneers (26-7) W
  • 2024, Week 7: New Orleans Saints (33-10) W
  • 2024, Week 8: Carolina Panthers (28-14) W
  • 2024, Week 11: Atlanta Falcons (38-6) W
  • 2025, Week 5: Philadelphia Eagles (21-17) W
  • 2025, Week 7: New York Giants (33-32) W
  • 2025, Week 8: Dallas Cowboys (44-24) W
  • 2025, Week 13: Washington Commanders (27-26) W
  • 2025, Week 15: Green Bay Packers (34-26) W

When asked about the streak, head coach Sean Payton smartly downplayed the whole thing noting the closeness of most of those games and how they just don’t play a whole lot of NFC teams.

“We’ve competed against some really good teams,” Payton said. “We’ve had some close NFC matchups. One that I remember is last year, the Eagles. They gave us a challenge, and we had to come back and same with the Giants. So we’ve had to play some complete football against these teams, and so I think it’s just by chance and by schedule. Obviously you play more AFC teams, usually typically year-to-year, so the pool is smaller. I think we’re playing good football when we play out of the league, but obviously that doesn’t win us the next game. So we just have to keep at it, and work hard out here on the field, practice hard and just get ready for the next one.”

I hate streaks and now that this one has been mentioned, I’ll be fretting every time they face an NFC opponent. To be fair, the NFC South was fairly bad in 2024 and the NFC East was not — which is why most of those games were wild and close comebacks wins for Denver. And it only got harder this season with the NFC West on the docket.

All streaks must end. Where do you think this one against NFC teams ends?

  • vs. Los Angeles Rams
  • at San Francisco 49ers
  • vs. Seattle Seahawks
  • at Arizona Cardinals
  • at Carolina Panthers

The first three on this list are no gimmies, but if I had to pick where the streak ends I would have to say on the road against the 49ers.

item.title: Saints vs. Raiders: Quarterback Matchup
item.description: Saints and Tyler Shough will face off against veteran QB Kirk Cousins but can the Saints force Mendoza into the game
item.content:encoded:
The Saints are set to finally host their home opener for the 2026 season against the Las Vegas Raiders in a matchup of two teams that have surprised the league through the first two weeks of the season.

The Raiders have former Saints OC Klint Kubiak as their new head coach, and through the first two weeks of the season, Kubiak has the Raiders humming as a team. The Raiders had the first overall pick and selected Fernando Mendoza, but Mendoza has yet to make a start. Instead, it’s been Kirk Cousins leading the charge for the Raiders.

Now, the Raiders have played against what may possibly be two of the worst teams in the NFL in the Dolphins and the Chargers, but the Raiders beat them, and Cousins played pretty well in both games. So far through two games, Cousins has completed 67.8% of his passes for 413 yards, 6 TDs, and 3 interceptions. He has also been sacked twice so far this season.

Cousins is very familiar with playing against the Saints and in the Dome, but this experience may be a little different. Being at home, the defense will want to pressure Cousins up the middle, and having a true home-field advantage will help with slowing down the offensive linemen from getting off the ball, especially on the edges.

Keep in mind, Cousins is a 15-year veteran, so fooling him will not be something that is easily accomplished. Blitzing for the sake of blitzing should not be the focus here. Instead, change what he sees post-snap and make the pressure feel like it’s always coming at him through simulated looks. If the rush can start making him hesitate, he will hold the ball and also start to force passes into tight windows, which could lead to increasing that already elevated interception number that he has.

Tyler Shough is coming into his first game as the captain of this team and is also coming off one of the biggest road victories this team has had in nearly half a decade. The Dome will be ready to celebrate the new face of the team, and deservedly so.

Shough is finding his groove. Shough is currently leading the NFL in several categories: passing yards with 662, completions with 62, 20-yard completions with 11, and passing yards per game with 331. He is also second in attempts with 90.

Through two games, Shough has 4 TDs and 2 INTs. The great thing about this is that both interceptions came in the Week 1 game against the Lions, and he was able to finish the game against the Ravens with 0 turnovers. Shough has to stay on this path and continue to limit the turnovers.

He will have a tough challenge this week, as starting LT Kelvin Banks Jr. will be out with a high ankle sprain, and the Raiders will feature Maxx Crosby, one of the league’s best pass rushers. So, protection will be at a premium.

The Saints will also have to get a run game going to support Shough, keep the linebackers and safeties off balance, and utilize the play-action game as an actual threat. Shough will also have to identify the coverage. The Raiders will feature a 3-4 base defense that will mix up which four defenders will rush.

Three keys to keep Shough rolling as one of the best QBs in the league for this game can be simplified to the three Ps: protection, patience, and play action.

This is a matchup of a very experienced veteran who is mentoring a future starter and a young, rising QB who is showcasing a little bit of superstar potential. Who will be the one who can come out on top in this matchup?

Can the Saints force the veteran to the bench and push Kubiak to put in the young rookie because they need a spark? That is very unlikely, especially on the road, but that was a situation Tyler Shough found himself in during the middle part of last season against the Rams.

Sunday will be a very fun game. Two teams that no one really had high expectations for will face off, and the Saints walk into this matchup with the edge at the QB position.

Who do you think will have the better game? What do you think the Saints should do to help elevate Shough and slow down Cousins?

item.title: Cowboys vs Ravens: 2 players Dallas should use more in Brazil
item.description: Which Cowboys do you think need to be getting more playing time?
item.content:encoded:
After a big-time win against the Washington Commanders last Sunday, the Dallas Cowboys travel out of the country this week to try to build a winning streak. Dallas will face the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil on Sunday.

Before the Cowboys and Ravens square off, here are two players Dallas should use more in this South American matchup.

1) ED Malachi Lawrence

The Cowboys made a big gamble this offseason, assuming that first-round pick Malachi Lawrence could be an impact pass rusher in his first NFL season. While Lawrence showed plenty of pass-rush potential in college, it’s hard for any edge defender to come in and be a consistent pass-rush threat right away.

Lawrence’s NFL career got off to a slow start with an uneventful performance in Week 1 against the Giants. To the 23-year-old’s credit, he only played 11 pass-rush snaps, so he wasn’t given much of a chance to make an impact. In Week 2 against the Commanders, Dallas upped Lawrence’s pass-rush opportunities, raising his pass-rush snaps in the game to 16.

The increased playing time led to an increase in production as Lawrence recorded three total pressures, two hurries, and a QB hit against Washington. Lawrence’s 74.6 Pro Football Focus pass rush grade was the highest of any Dallas defender, as was his 33.3% Win%.

Facing off against a talented Ravens offense this week, led by superstar quarterback Lamar Jackson, the Cowboys need to give Lawrence even more opportunities to get after the quarterback. Getting to Jackson, and ultimately getting hits on him, will be a top priority if Dallas wants to walk out of Brazil with a win. 

He may not be a complete player just yet, but Lawrence is clearly one of Dallas’ best pass-rush threats at the moment and should be treated as such.

2) WR George Pickens

After a career year in 2025, George Pickens has gotten off to a bit of a slow start this season. Through two games, Pickens has caught nine passes for 68 yards, an average of 7.6 Y/R, and is yet to find the end zone. On Pickens nine receptions, he is yet to record a catch of more than 12 yards, something very uncharacteristic for his game.

Last week against the Commanders, Pickens saw limited opportunities as CeeDee Lamb was the focal point of Dallas’ offensive attack. On Sunday against a much more talented Ravens defense, the Cowboys will need to get Pickens going alongside Lamb if they want to walk out of Brazil with a victory. The Ravens gave up three receptions of 20+ yards against the Saints last week, so Pickens should have a chance to make some big plays,

Whether it’s getting him a chance to make plays deep down the field or getting the ball in his hands quickly with a chance to run after, Dallas must push the ball to Pickens on Sunday and get him involved early and often.

item.title: Opponent Breakdown: Wake Forest Defense
item.description: Wake Forest has started this season with three strong performances, led by a defense that has done well to contain opposing offenses. While their offense has gotten a lot of focus, the Deacs have flown under the radar on the defensive side of the ball. The start to the Miami game was bad, to say […]
item.content:encoded:
Wake Forest has started this season with three strong performances, led by a defense that has done well to contain opposing offenses. While their offense has gotten a lot of focus, the Deacs have flown under the radar on the defensive side of the ball. The start to the Miami game was bad, to say the least, but the defense regrouped and held a Miami offense that could be the best in the country in check in the second half. This group will get another test this week as Louisville’s offense has been piling up points and yardage at will this year.

Langston Hardy and Gabe Kirschke are the key players up front for Wake, and they man the edge spots for the defense. Hardy is the son of former Illinois great Kevin Hardy, while Kirschke leads the team in pressures with 8 this season. Both players were lauded with preseason accolades, and they have both started the season well. Kirschke has been outstanding, and the Cards will have to account for him as a run defender as well as when he rushes the passer.

The Deacs are a little undersized up front, but that works for their defensive scheme as they look to create havoc with their front four. Dallas Afalava is the main man in the middle of the defense. He plays the 3-technique, which allows him to do what he does best, which is shoot gaps and get into the backfield. He has done a good job collapsing pockets as a pass rusher, and he holds up against the run as well. Louisville will get another good test to see if their success running the ball against SMU can be sustainable.

Wake runs into issues on defense once you get past the front four. While this defense has played well, opposing offenses have essentially been playing 7-on-7 against their pass defense. That starts at linebacker, where Frank Cusano and Aiden Hall have had no success stopping the pass. The defense as a whole has only seen 14 passes not be completed. For context, Lincoln Keinholz had 11 incompletions against Ole Miss and 9 against SMU. The linebackers are struggling in coverage, but they do a solid job against the run, with Vincent Firenze being an efficient playmaker when he’s in the game.

While the secondary is pretty much allowing opposing quarterbacks to throw against air, they have done a very good job of containing explosive plays. Wake has only allowed 5 passes for more than 10 yards this season, and no completions have gone for 30 yards. It’s as if they have a forefield behind the defense. They force everything short and once the pass is completed, they get downhill to make the tackle. More than half of the passing yards they’ve given up are after the catch, because quarterbacks are taking what is given to them. It’s a good strategy, but I’ve never seen it work this well.

The plan has worked well for them, but the Deacs are giving up 235 yards per game through the air, and they don’t have an interception yet. Malachi Toney had a field day in the first half last weekend because he is electric after the catch. While Lawayne McCoy and Tre Richardson are not Toney, they have both shown that they can be dynamic with the ball in their hands. It will be fascinating to see if the Wake game plan will work against the Cards.

item.title: Week 3 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Cowboys and Ravens set for a great matchup in Brazil
item.description: The Ravens and Cowboys both come into Week 3 with 1-1 records.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL is investing a lot into its international series, which is clear from this week's matchup in Brazil.

The league's most marketable team, the Dallas Cowboys, gets to face a Baltimore Ravens team that has Super Bowl hopes and one of the most marketable players in Lamar Jackson. It's a great matchup for Rio de Janeiro. The NFL booked some top-tier matchups for other countries this season, and this might be the best of the group.

The fear is the turf at Maracanã Stadium. There was enough concern that the NFL's field director commented on it this week to ESPN and said the league isn't concerned. That doesn't mean it will be a perfect surface or close to it. There has been a lot of rain in Rio de Janeiro over the past six weeks and soccer players have complained about the turf. For two fast offenses, that could be a big factor.

The Cowboys defense could use the help. Dallas looked better in Week 2, but still allowed 389 yards even though Washington lost Jayden Daniels on the final play of the first half. The offense will be good, though maybe not quite as good if the turf in Brazil is poor. It's the defense Dallas needs to worry about.

There is some concern about the Ravens' offense if receiver Zay Flowers can't play through a hamstring injury, and Baltimore will surely be careful if the turf is bad. But Jackson will make it work against a Dallas defense that is still suspect. The Cowboys' defensive issues are the main reason why Ravens -3.5 is the pick. Hopefully the conditions in Brazil don't bother what looks like a phenomenal matchup on Sunday.

Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 3 of the NFL season:

Packers (-5) over Falcons

It's not fun to pick the Packers right now. They're beat up on offense, especially the offensive line. That's a reason this line moved down from Packers -7.5. But it's not like the Falcons are good. Sure, getting Michael Penix Jr. back helps. But Penix hasn't been great in his career and he's playing his first game action since Nov. 16, 2025. It's hard to have a lot of trust in him or the Falcons.

Jaguars (-3) over Patriots

It's not too surprising the Jaguars faded in the second half last week at Denver. Playing in altitude early in the season is not easy. The Jaguars are a good team. Are the Patriots? Probably, but staying in their offensive funk last week against the Steelers wasn't promising. The Jaguars look like the better team.

Giants (-2.5) over Titans

Teams using their backup quarterback often get a short-term bump. And while Jameis Winston has his flaws and didn't look good on Monday night, he is one of the NFL's more capable backups. While the Titans did play well against the Eagles last week, I'm not convinced they've turned a corner.

Chiefs (-11.5) over Dolphins

If you've followed these picks over the years, you haven't seen many double-digit road favorites being the pick. Teams facing the 2026 Dolphins might be an exception. The Dolphins haven't shown anything yet that would make anyone believe they are going to be competitive in many games this season. Maybe the Dolphins get a jolt in their home opener, but it's not a team that's showing any signs of life yet.

Bengals (-3.5) over Steelers

Speaking of teams that haven't shown anything yet, the Steelers are 1-1 and are lucky they played the Falcons in Week 1. There are two teams that have just one offensive touchdown this season: Pittsburgh and Atlanta. The Falcons have the excuse that they were down to their third- and then fourth-string quarterbacks. The Steelers have mostly used their preferred lineup. They just haven't been very good. The Bengals offense hasn't heated up yet, but it will, and the defense looks greatly improved. Dexter Lawrence II is a fun dark horse NFL Defensive Player of the Year candidate.

Commanders (+7) over Seahawks

The last time we saw this matchup in Landover, Md., the Seahawks blew out the Commanders 38-14 last season. And Jayden Daniels played most of that game before dislocating his elbow. Daniels is probably going to miss this week after dislocating his elbow again, and the Seahawks defense looks like it might be even better than last season. So why pick a Marcus Mariota-led Commanders team to cover? Ugly dogs cover all the time in the NFL, and you won't know many people picking Washington here.

Chargers (+7) over Bills

If there are any signs of life in the Chargers this season, we'll see it Sunday. They've been awful. But this line first opened at Bills -3 and jumped up four points the last couple weeks. It's justified based on how both teams have looked so far. But it is also a reminder that the full touchdown is a lot. The Chargers are entering an excruciating part of their schedule and have to know that it's now or never if they're going to save their season.

Panthers (-2.5) over Browns

Maybe what we saw from Deshaun Watson last week was a sign that he'll be just fine as Browns quarterback. It seems more like the Buccaneers defense was that bad in the second half. If Watson does it again, hats off to him. The Panthers have gotten off to a hot start, and part of that is playing the Bears' and Falcons' defenses. But don't forget how Jacksonville torched the Browns' defense in Week 1. Bryce Young might keep his good start going.

Texans (-2.5) over Colts

I'm 0-2 in trusting Houston this season, but undeterred. Houston will play well this season. The defense was very good last week, but the offense wasn't. That should change against a Colts defense that has given up 1,029 yards (!!!) in two games.

Jets (+6.5) over Lions

The Jets haven't been bad this season. They just couldn't finish last week against the Packers. And the Lions defense looks like it might keep every opponent in the game. Even if the Lions look good here, the defense allowing a backdoor cover will stay in play.

Buccaneers (+1.5) over Vikings

Get ready to handle the blitz, Buccaneers. The Vikings and their defensive coordinator Brian Flores are blitzing on over 80% of opponents' dropbacks so far this season. And it's working. But this is just the time when a 2-0 Vikings team is favored on the road against an 0-2 Buccaneers team and it looks so easy to pick Minnesota. The Buccaneers are the more desperate team and got embarrassed last week losing to the Browns, and unless you believe they have given up on Todd Bowles already, that's generally the type of team worth backing.

Cardinals (+8.5) over 49ers

Maybe the Chargers are simply putrid. But don't forget that in Week 1, the Cardinals were a 9.5-point underdog against the Chargers and went on the road and won. It's doubtful that they're beating the 49ers straight up, but as long as they're not facing the Seahawks defense they should be able to move the ball.

Saints (-3) over Raiders

This point spread might be too little respect for the Saints, or a lot for the Raiders. The Saints are a missed two-point conversion away from beating the Lions and Ravens on the road to start the season. They might be good. The Raiders are much improved too. Picking the Saints isn't necessarily a fade of the Raiders, but acknowledging how impressive New Orleans' start has been.

Rams (-2.5) over Broncos

The Broncos have played two good quarters out of eight. The Rams were a no-show in Week 1, but as they were pounding the Giants in Week 2 it sure looked like we can excuse that performance to a weird Australia trip and weirder travel plan for it. Part of that travel plan was presumably to not be impacted through September by jet lag, and that might have worked. Historically, the Broncos are good at home in September and they're not a bad team. But maybe what we saw Monday night was the first sign of the Rams being the team they were hyped up to be before the season.

Eagles (-4.5) over Bears

It's hard to know if Caleb Williams will play. If he does, then Bears +4.5 is an easy play. But the Bears could be down to Case Keenum against a talented Eagles defense. And if Williams does play, will he be fully mobile with his hamstring injury? The safe play is to take the Eagles, though they have not been impressive despite a 2-0 start.

Last week: 7-9

Season to date: 14-18
