item.title: 2026 NFL Week 3: Hart’s Picks
item.description: Mile High Report’s Christopher Hart predicts the straight-up winners for every Week 3 matchup of the 2026 season.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome back to the third installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. For Week 1, I was 11-5 with my predictions. Unfortunately, my Week 2 predictions were worse at 9-7. Let’s see if I can get back on track with my Week 3 picks.

Atlanta Falcons at Green Bay Packers — Thursday Night Football

Michael Penix Jr. will lead the Falcons on the gridiron against the Packers on Thursday Night Football. While I’m not thrilled with how the Packers have looked defensively, the Falcons only have 16 points on offense in two contests thus far. Green Bay should take care of business at home.

Winner: Packers

Houston Texans at Indianapolis Colts — Sunday (Early Game)

Both the Texans and Colts enter Week 3 winless. Neither defense is playing at a high level, and each have their own issues on the offensive side of the ball. With Alec Pierce out, Indianapolis will have to rely on Jonathan Taylor to dominate on the ground. And the Texans need to figure out something with their ground game after last week’s performance.

Winner: Texans

New England Patriots at Jacksonville Jaguars — Sunday (Early Game)

The Patriots rebounded in Week 2, whilst the Jaguars ended up cratering in the second half versus the Broncos. New England has played well defensively thus far, but they still have some kinks to work out on offense. Overall, I think the Jaguars bounce back after their loss to the Broncos and find a way to defeat the Patriots at home.

Winner: Jaguars

Cincinnati Bengals at Pittsburgh Steelers — Sunday (Early Game)

The Bengals enter this AFC North matchup at 2-0 with the chance to start to pull away from several division competitors with a win on Sunday. They have looked a lot better on defense compared to last season. The Steelers are struggling to get anything going offensively with just 23 points in two outings thus far. I like Cincinnati in this one as road victors.

Winner: Bengals

Los Angeles Chargers at Buffalo Bills — Sunday (Early Game)

Quite simply, nothing is going right for the Chargers to begin the season. They’re 0-2 with a defense that has experienced a big dropoff and a Mike McDaniel offense that continues to have growing pains. Even worse, they just lost tight ends David Njoku and Charlie Kollar and starting left guard Kayode Awosika to injury. I can’t see any reasonable way they topple Josh Allen and the Bills on the road. I’m taking Buffalo at home.

Winner: Bills

Carolina Panthers at Cleveland Browns — Sunday (Early Game)

After Week 1 losses, both of these teams secured much-needed victories in Week 2. Both defenses are still struggling, but the Panthers offense led by Bryce Young is scoring a lot of points. I think that will be the key difference in this matchup. I’ll take Carolina on the road.

Winner: Panthers

New York Jets at Detroit Lions — Sunday (Early Game)

Speaking of bad defense play, the Lions have been absolutely atrocious to start the season. If they can’t find a way to get that side of the ball fixed, they could be in for a long and disappointing season. That being said, I’m not sure the Jets will be able to do enough to limit Detroit’s offense in a road game, so I’ll be picking the Lions in this one.

Winner: Lions

Seattle Seahawks at Washington Commanders — Sunday (Early Game)

It’s hard to envision a Commanders team without Jayden Daniels being able to topple the defending champion Seattle Seahawks. Seattle’s defense has been playing extremely well and Drew Lock is doing enough as their starting quarterback to help win games. I think they move to 3-0 on the season and beat Washington at home.

Winner: Seahawks

Kansas City Chiefs at Miami Dolphins — Sunday (Early Game)

The Chiefs were able to topple the Colts in overtime in Week 2, while the Dolphins dropped to 0-2 on the season. As I wrote during Week 1, I think Miami could wind up having to top pick in this year’s draft. They are not a good football team. That’s why I expect the Chiefs to get the road victory and go to 3-0 on the season.

Winner: Chiefs

Tennessee Titans at New York Giants — Sunday (Early Game)

After an impressive win to start the season, the Giants were blown out by the Rams on Monday night. Jaxson Dart was injured and their running game struggled. Truth be told, the Titans are 0-2 and have a lot of issues. Perhaps there is an opening here to get their first win because of the Giants not having Dart. I’ll roll the dice on Tennessee here, but that’s operating under the big assumption they can stop the run and Cam Ward plays better than he has the first two weeks.

Winner: Titans

Arizona Cardinals at San Francisco 49ers — Sunday (Afternoon Game)

The 49ers are 2-0 and the Cardinals are 1-1. All things considered, the 49ers are performing well on offense and have a very staunch defense to match. With a great coaching staff, that’s a recipe to win a lot of football games. I expect them to do just that on Sunday against the Cardinals.

Winners: 49ers

Minnesota Vikings at Tampa Bay Buccaneers — Sunday (Afternoon Game)

The Vikings defense, led by Brian Flores, continues to impress. However, their offense will remain to be a work in progress until their quarterback situation stabilizes. It appears Kyler Murray will return this week. Maybe that can be the spark they need. As for Tampa Bay, they are 0-2 and facing a must-win matchup in this one. I can’t think of many teams in recent memory that have started off 0-3 and wound up making the playoffs. Will that be enough motivation to get Baker Mayfield and company a win? I’m not so sure about that. I’ll be taking the Vikings on the road.

Winner: Vikings

Baltimore Ravens at Dallas Cowboys — Sunday (Afternoon Game)

This may be one of the most interesting matchups of the week. It’ll be played in Rio De Janeiro, Brazil. Both of these teams are 1-1 and have similar production on offense and defense. I think whatever team does the best with their rushing attack will end up finding a way to win. The Ravens should just feed Derrick Henry. That usually winds up working for them. I’ll take Baltimore in this international affair.

Winner: Ravens

Las Vegas Raiders at New Orleans Saints — Sunday (Afternoon Game)

Surprise! The Raiders are 2-0 to start the season. How many folks predicted that? On the other hand, the Saints are 1-1. Tyler Shough has shown some promise in his second season with New Orleans. They need more effectiveness from Travis Etienne, who was their big free agent signing at running back. I’ll take the Saints at home.

Winner: Saints

Los Angeles Rams at Denver Broncos — Sunday Night Football

This is one of the best matchups of the weekend. Matthew Stafford was the NFL MVP last season and is coming off a really good performance and a rebound victory. The same goes for the Broncos, who found a way to embark on an impressive comeback against the Jaguars. I think this is going to be a very close game. I’m picking Denver here.

Winner: Broncos

Philadelphia Eagles at Chicago Bears — Monday Night Football

With Caleb Williams being out and the Bears likely having to start Case Keenum at quarterback, this game became a lot easier for me to predict. I’ll be taking the Eagles on the road on MNF. I just can’t envision Keenum being able to best a Vic Fangio defense in primetime.

Winner: Eagles

item.title: Ravens news: Lamar Jackson could run all over Cowboys defense
item.description: Rounding up the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover Lamar Jackson’s major rushing opportunity against the Cowboys, early-season results of past Super Bowl champions, and first-round pick Vega Ioane’s Week 2 grades. Let’s dive in!

Lamar Jackson could run all over Cowboys defense

On Sunday in Brazil, the NFL’s worst rushing defense against quarterbacks will go up against the most dangerous rushing quarterback in league history. Hammer, meet nail.

Lamar Jackson has gashed the Cowboys on the ground before. In their previous two matchups, he has racked up 181 yards and two touchdowns on 23 carries (6.7 yards per carry) – not to mention a 120.44 passer rating, 9.03 yards per attempt, and three more scores through the air. Dallas, meanwhile, allowed Jaxson Dart to rush for 54 yards on 11 attempts in Week 1 and surrendered 69 yards to Jayden Daniels in the first half of Week 2.

The two-time MVP has yet to take over a game with his legs this year. New offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has prioritized an under-center rushing attack with play-action looks that get Jackson on the move as a passer. This is part of an intentional effort to keep the Ravens away from the shotgun-based hero-ball trap the offense has fallen in for years. But…that big red button is always there. On an international trip, while dealing with injuries, and against a defense that has struggled against mobile quarterbacks, Doyle may want to consider breaking out his not-so-secret weapon this week.

Kenny Clark, Donovan Ezeiruaku break down facing Lamar Jackson, Ravens offense – Tommy Yarrish (DallasCowboys.com)

Ravens QB and two-time league MVP Lamar Jackson awaits in Brazil, a difficult challenge for any team because of his ability to break contain and make explosive plays with his legs. The Cowboys defense understands the task that lies ahead in containing Jackson.

“We all know what it is,” Cowboys OLB Donovan Ezeiruaku said. “You guys know. We know as players the type of guy he is. Somebody who can throw the ball, but also run the ball at a very high level. It’s easier to say than to do, but our job is to go out there and go do. That’s what we’re tasked with.”

Past Super Bowl champs rarely defined by early-season loss

Super Bowl odds: Bills now clear No. 2, plus what history tells us about 1-1 Ravens – Scott Phillips (The Athletic)

Of the 14 teams currently carrying Super Bowl odds shorter than +2500 on BetMGM, eight of them hold at least one loss, including the favorite Rams at No. 1 and the Ravens at No. 3. Although it might feel like a September dud would deflate Super Bowl chances, recent history shows it’s fairly normal for future champions to lose early in the season. Six of the last 10 Super Bowl champions started the regular season 1-1 — including the last three winners…

Week 2 grades for 1st-round pick Vega Ioane

Grading all 32 NFL first-round rookies after Week 2 – Dalton Wasserman (Pro Football Focus)

Overall Rookie Grade: 61.1 (Rank: 5/12)

Principal Opponent: Vernon Broughton

Week 2 Snaps: 58

Week 2 Grade: 47.7

Ioane took a slight step back from his solid Week 1 performance, earning a 47.7 PFF grade that was the lowest along Baltimore’s offensive line this week. He allowed four pressures, all hurries, in pass protection, which brings his total to six for the season. Ioane still flashed his potential as a run-blocker as he generated four positive, but also four negative, grades in that department.

item.title: Inside the matchup: How Commanders can defy odds, best the Seahawks in Week 3
item.description: The winless Commanders host the undefeated Seahawks in a key Week 3 NFC contest
item.content:encoded:
Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates as we go inside the matchup to get you ready for every opponent the Commanders face in 2026.

From John Portis:

Bill-in-Bangkok was certainly right back in June, when he originally evaluated this Commanders-Seahawks matchup. A lot has changed since the initial preview. His write-up hits close to home, as Washington enters Week 3 with quarterback Jayden Daniels sidelined by yet another elbow dislocation and Marcus Mariota once again behind center.

The Seahawks are expected to start their own backup quarterback, Drew Lock, though it should be noted that Sam Darnold practiced in a limited capacity on Wednesday. It’s at least possible that Darnold could be available.

Lock has performed well in Darnold’s absence, completing 35-of-48 passes for 422 passing yards, four touchdowns, and no interceptions in two games. Three of those touchdowns went to receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba last week versus the Cardinals, and the prospect of facing him with a Commanders’ secondary that will be already be missing Nick Cross should keep coordinator Daronte Jones up at night. If the Commanders’ defense can somehow contain JSN, they will be left with Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed in the passing game.

Rookie running back Jadarian Price is recovering from a shoulder injury and may miss the game — time will tell on that front — but free agent-signing Emanuel Wilson, who spent 3 seasons with the Packers, has been a solid addition to the Seahawks backfield and will work alongside last year’s undrafted free agent signing George Holani, who is dealing with a knee issue.

Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury, who utilizes an outside zone rushing scheme, has leaned on the run with Darnold out, running the ball over half the time with 55.4% running plays to 44.6% passing.

Washington has been surprisingly good in run defense, stuffing 29% for no gain, which ranks 3rd overall, with defensive lineman Javon Kinlaw ranking 3rd in the NFL in individual rankings of run stop rate.

The real strength of the Seahawks is head coach Mike Macdonald’s defense. They have continued their outstanding play from 2025 as outlined by Bill in his preview, and the Seahawks are the first team since 2006 not to allow a play of 20-plus yards through two weeks. Second-round safety Bud Clark broke his ankle in preseason, and Coby Bryant left in free agency. First-round safety Nick Emmanwori returned on a limited basis last week, playing eight defensive snaps, and was a full participant on Wednesday. He seems in line to play on Sunday, but we will see.

Meanwhile, free safety Julian Love has been making a case to be considered an elite player.

Washington offensive coordinator David Blough will have his hands full, and so will Washington’s embattled interior offensive line, which is likely to be without starting right guard Sam Cosmi, who is in the concussion protocol. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams continues to play at a high level, along with the rest of the defensive line.

The prospective hope for a Commanders win lies in quarterback Marcus Mariota’s ability to read defenses and get the ball out quickly to short and intermediate parts of the field. Another lies in Drew Lock’s past history of inconsistent play. He’s a gunslinger prototype at the quarterback position, and has a career completion rate of 60.2% with over 28 career interceptions in 29 starts. Through two games, the Commanders’ defense has forced zero turnovers, which is a statistic that will need to change if Washington wants a chance to win their first game of the season at Northwest Stadium this Sunday.

Betting Lines

Oddsmakers have established the visitors as the favorites for this matchup.

  • Point Spread: Seattle -7
  • Game Total (Over/Under): 40.5 points

Bill-in-Bangkok’s original preview published June 28:

Week 3 Preview: Seattle Seahawks at Washington Commanders

Date: September 28, 2026, 1 p.m. ET
Location: Northwest Stadium in Landover Maryland

After road games in Weeks 1 & 2 against a pair of hated division rivals, the Commanders will return home in Week 3 to face the Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 3. No easy games to open the 2026 season! A lot could change by the time these two teams meet, but it’s no surprise that the early betting lines favor the Seahawks on the road against the Commanders.

The All-Time Series Numbers

While these two teams wouldn’t seem to be natural rivals, they have played one another 24 times since Seattle joined the league as an expansion team in the mid-1970s. Washington leads the overall series 13-11-0, and the burgundy & gold has won 8 of 15 games played in this millennium.

The Seahawks have prevailed in the postseason, however. The two teams met in the playoffs three times between the 2005 and 2012 seasons, with Seattle sweeping the Redskins by winning all 3 games — none by less than 10 points.

Interestingly, Washington has been more successful as the road team in recent years, losing 4 out of the last 5 games played in Landover while winning 3 of the last 5 games played in Seattle.

Commanders quarterback play and health has been an issue at times

I’m sure everyone will remember the gruesome-looking play in which Jayden Daniels suffered a dislocated left elbow in the fourth quarter of the Week 9 game against the Seattle Seahawks at Northwest Stadium.

A similarly gruesome-looking knee injury ended the rookie season of Robert Griffin III against the Seahawks in the playoff game at Landover in January 2013.

In the three Seattle-Washington games played between those two injuries, Washington’s offense was led by Dwayne Haskins (2020), Taylor Heinicke (2021) and Sam Howell (2023), which may help explain the .250 win percentage under Ron Rivera and Dan Quinn.

Hopefully, Jayden Daniels can put an end to this streak of quarterback infamy and injury with a complete and winning effort in Week 3.

Seahawks quarterback stability

Seattle’s starting quarterback is Sam Darnold. Not so long ago, that would have been a reason for many NFL fans to scoff, but Darnold has just finished back-to-back Pro Bowl seasons with the Vikings and Seahawks, and he has a shiny new championship ring.

Like last year, Darnold is backed up by Drew Lock and Jalen Milroe.

Seahawks 2026 Coaching Changes

*New to staff this season:

  • Offensive Coordinator – Brian Fleury
  • Offensive Line – John Benton
  • Running Backs – Thomas Hammock
  • Inside Linebackers – Zach Orr
  • Quarterbacks – Tyson Prince

The Seahawks coaching staff changes could be significant. Sam Darnold will have both a new offensive coordinator and a new quarterback coach. Fleury comes from 7 seasons with the 49ers; Prince is a 4th year coach who has moved up quickly in Seattle after one year in the college ranks.

Add in John Benton’s promotion to senior offensive assistant & offensive line coach, and we could see a very different Seahawks offense in 2026. Fleury’s offensive scheme will be a highly structured, modern variant of the Shanahan-style West Coast offense, built on wide-zone running, heavy pre-snap motion, and calculated deep shots — which may sound familiar to fans who have been reading up on Commanders’ new offensive coordinator David Blough. Upon taking the job, Fleury declared that his unit would be “fast, violent, and aggressive in every way we possibly can” to pressure opponents both structurally and through variable tempo.

Their first-round pick in the backfield, Jadarian Price from Notre Dame, will have a new running backs coach in Thomas Hammock.

One of the most underrated moves of the entire NFL offseason is also on this list, though, with the Seahawks adding former Ravens defensive coordinator Zach Orr as inside linebackers coach. The wealth of defensive knowledge between head coach Mike Macdonald and Orr should pay off handsomely for the Seahawks; a scary thought given that the Seahawks had the #1 defense in points-allowed in 2026.

Key statistical 2025 rankings

Offensive Rankings

Under coordinator Klint Kubiak, the offense was a top-tier scoring unit that prioritized high yards-per-play efficiency:

  • Scoring Offense: 3rd overall (28.4 points per game)
  • Total Offense: 7th overall (351.4 total yards per game)
  • Offensive DVOA: 9th overall (9.2%)
  • Passing DVOA: 5th overall (32.2%)
  • Rushing DVOA: 13th overall (-2.2%)
  • Yards Per Play: 2nd overall (5.6 yards per play)

Defensive Rankings

Head coach Mike Macdonald’s defense was statistically the best in the NFL, finishing as a top-10 historic defense in modern analytics:

  • Scoring Defense: 1st overall (17.2 points allowed per game)
  • Total Defense: 1st overall (285.8 yards allowed per game)
  • Overall Defensive DVOA: 1st overall (-24.0% — ranked 8th all-time in NFL history)
  • Passing Defense DVOA: 1st overall (-19.2%)
  • Rushing Defense DVOA: 1st overall (-30.7%)
  • Opponent Yards Per Play: 1st overall (4.4 yards allowed per play)

Roster Moves: Free Agency and the Draft

Key Free Agent Signings/Departures

* SIGNED IN FREE AGENCY

  • LB Dante Fowler Jr.
  • LB Chazz Surratt (Re-signed)
  • CB Noah Igbinoghene
  • RB Emanual Wilson
  • WR Jake Bobo (Re-signed)
  • OL Josh Jones (Re-signed)
  • CB Josh Jobe (Re-signed)
  • WR Rashid Shaheed (Re-signed)

* DEPARTED IN FREE AGENCY

  • RB Kenneth Walker III
  • LB Boye Mafe
  • S Coby Bryant
  • CB Riq Woolen

The Seahawks put a heavy emphasis on re-signing their own free agents this offseason, which gives them a short list of departures; nonetheless, they are all significant. Coby Bryant played 100% of the team’s defensive snaps in the Super Bowl, while Riq Woolen and Boye Mafe were contributors as well. Of course, Kenneth Walker was the Super Bowl MVP.

Seattle did add former Commanders pass rusher in Dante Fowler Jr. to pair with DeMarcus Lawrence, and they used the draft to help maintain depth in the secondary that was key to their defensive success last year. Another element of that depth comes in the form of the free agent signing of former Washington CB Noah Igbinoghene, who may struggle to make the 53-man roster in Seattle.

As discussed above, their offensive core of Sam Darnold, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashid Shaheed, and Cooper Kupp will have a new rookie running back and new play-caller in Brian Fleury, replacing Klint Kubiak who parlayed winning a Super Bowl with this group into the head coaching job with the Raiders.

The 2026 NFL Draft

Round 1, No. 32: Jadarian Price (RB, Notre Dame)
Explosive runner and high-end kickoff returner; co-RB1 replacement for departed Kenneth Walker III. Should fit perfectly into Seattle’s outside-zone rushing scheme.

Round 2, No. 64: Bud Clark (S, TCU)
Experienced, highly competitive, versatile defensive ball hawk who will compete immediately at safety. Plays with a physical edge reminiscent of Devon Witherspoon.

Round 3, No. 99: Julian Neal (CB, Arkansas)
Tall, physical corner (nearly 6’2″) who loves to hit and press receivers. He is a good candidate to step in as Seattle’s 3rd CB.

Round 5, No. 148: Beau Stephens (OG, Iowa)
Versatile 1st-team All-American; expected to push incumbent Anthony Bradford for the starting RG spot.

Round 6, No. 199: Emmanuel Henderson Jr. (WR, Kansas)
Speedy WR; valuable kickoff coverage and return experience. Depth and special teams.

Round 7, No. 236: Andre Fuller (CB, Toledo)
A safety-to-corner convert with good size and 4.49 speed. Depth and battle for one of the remaining CB spots.

Round 7, No. 242: Deven Eastern (DT, Minnesota)
Experienced, durable interior lineman; started 39 college games. Will help restock and add youth to the Seahawks aging defensive line pipeline.

Round 7, No. 255: Michael Dansby (CB, Arizona)
Smaller, faster man-coverage CB; strong candidate for practice squad.

The Dallas Cowboys have the luxury of having CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens at wide receiver, but more importantly, they are rooting for each other to succeed. In Week 2, the Cowboys looked better in some ways against the Commanders. However, the Ravens will be a much stronger challenge in Brazil this Sunday.

Getting the defensive unit clicking on all cylinders will take some time, but several rookies have stepped up to take the reins. Dalla was able to even their record at 1-1 last week, but things like the lack of a consistent running game still need to be addressed.

Cowboys’ CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens playing with ‘no egos’ – Todd Archer, ESPN

Lamb and Pickens already had a relationship before the latter made it to Dallas. That has helped them form a selfless bond with one another.

“I don’t think you can get any much closer than we’ve been,” Lamb said. “I feel like at the end of the day, we want what’s best for each other and that’s to be with one another and to grind.

“I feel like we both have that alpha mentality, that alpha dog component to us so just rubbing off on one another and just keeping this thing going. We gotta keep being who we are and at the end of the day prove it to each other every day.”

Cowboys’ evolving defense faces tough questions, difficult challenge in Ravens’ offense – Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News

Dallas is on Year 1 under Christian Parker as defensive coordinator, and they’re currently working the kinks out. On Sunday, the Ravens will present their biggest test yet.

What the Ravens possess — an elusive quarterback in Lamar Jackson, an elite running back Derrick Henry along with a strong offensive line  — seem like dangerous items for the Cowboys defense to handle.

On the season, the Ravens have rushed for 310 yards (fourth-most in the league) with a 5.3 average (third-best in the league). Henry, despite limited work in the second half of the loss to the Saints in Week 2, averages 5.3 yards per carry.

The Cowboys’ defense allows 5 yards per carry. 

Cowboys riding the wave of 3 rookies on defense: ‘They don’t repeat mistakes’ – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram

Defense was a major issue for the Cowboys coming into this season. In the first two games, three rookies on that side of the ball are leading the way.

In fact, there are more encouraging signs that the Cowboys defense is simply a work-in-progress rather than a lost hope. Among those, three rookies have found key roles on defensive coordinator Christian Parker’s unit: defensive back Caleb Downs, outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence and inside linebacker Jaishawn Barham.

While Downs was the only one among those three to start both games for the Cowboys, Lawrence has played 38-percent of snaps in key pass rush situations and Barham has filled in as the starting green-dot linebacker in the absence of DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring strain).

3 pressing questions following Cowboys’ season-saving win over Commanders – Jess Haynie, The Landry Hat

It wasn’t pretty, but Dallas was able to beat Washington last Sunday. However, several questions still need answers.

What’s wrong with the run game?

Dallas has yet to crack 4.0 yards-per-carry in either game this year. For an offense that averaged 4.6 in 2025 and brought back every starter and coach, this early-season stagnation is surprising and, after two weeks, increasingly concerning.

The easy answer is LG Tyler Smith’s absence, which will extend through at least Week 4. Going from Smith to T.J. Bass is certainly a detriment to the rushing attack, but would Brian Schottenheimer and Klayton Adams be smart to lay this entirely at Bass’ feet?

Jaishawn Barham looked the part for the Cowboys, but he’s got an urgent problem to fix to reach full potential – Mauricio Rodriguez, AtoZ Sports

Barham had a great bounce-back performance in Week 2 after struggling in his NFL debut. With that said, one thing is holding him back from being even better.

Barham briefly had to exit the game to be checked out by trainers. Later in the game, he was seen puking before a play, missing most of the game after that.

With Barham being one of the best defenders from Week 2, the Cowboys need him to play as much as possible. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer was asked about his conditioning on Wednesday.

“Young player, he has been working actually pretty hard on it,” Schottenheimer said of the rookie’s conditioning. “The best way to get in shape is to play, so he’s working through that.”

Labeled a Cowboys’ Bust, Tyler Guyton is Growing Before our Eyes in 2026 – Cody Warren, Inside The Star

Guyton has been looking for the consistency in his game since he was drafted in the first round in 2024. He’s gradually doing just that this season.

We watched a rookie year marred with penalties and inconsistency, but the penalties were the biggest headache as he committed 18 of them that year.

It seemed like every time the offense did something right, we would see a yellow flag lying on the ground near the offensive line and we knew it was Guyton.

18 penalties is a brutal number for any offensive lineman, especially your starting left tackle. You can survive a bad rep now and then, you can survive pressure, but one thing a young offensive lineman can’t keep doing is wiping out good plays.

item.description: New York Giants headlines for Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories as the Giants get set to battle the Tennessee Titans this Sunday.

Vaccaro: Jaxson Dart’s Broadway tale staring down a cruel reality | New York Post

Jaxson Dart was the one. He was the heir. In this 50th year since Broadway Joe Namath took his talents to Los Angeles for the final forgettable chapter of his career, New York has long sought the successor to the character Namath created and no one else had seen fit to copy: the big-city QB1 who liked the bright lights as much as the lights love him.

Tiki: Giants have to consider all options at QB

Politi: Jaxson Dart’s injury will force Giants to make a crucial QB decision … again | NJ.com

A franchise quarterback must prove he can stay on the field, and between this injury and his frequent trips to the blue medical tent as a rookie, there is no evidence that Dart can pass that test. No one is questioning the former Ole Miss passer’s toughness, and sure, Dart might prove to be a stable, 17-game starter with better luck (and decent blocking).

The Giants’ braintrust can’t count on that, though, especially not when Dart hasn’t proven that he is the guy in his short career and not when this is a rare draft loaded with top-end quarterback talent.

O’Connor: It’s a Dart disaster for Giants. Time for John Harbaugh to earn his $100 million | The Athletic

That’s why the 2026 Giants season is already locked in a life-and-death struggle. As one of the best coaches of his generation, John Harbaugh was worth the $100 million investment the Giants made in him. He will earn all of that cash this year if he can somehow keep his team breathing.

All Giants eyes on John Harbaugh now, and that’s the way it should be | The Record

John Harbaugh raises the floor for an entire franchise and Jaxson Dart raises the ceiling. If you’re the New York Giants today, especially a fan base that has come to expect the worst for a decade-plus, you can’t help but feeling like the ceiling just caved in on the season and so much more.

Willie Colon sees a path for the Giants

With Jaxson Dart Out For The Year, Giants Should Ride The Jameis Winston Wave | FOX Sports

Which is why it’s Winston-or-bust for this star-crossed team in 2026. The Giants will say that’s not so bad. After all, they liked Winston enough to sign him to a two-year, $13 million contract extension just two weeks ago, making him one of the highest-paid backup QBs in the league.

But their faith in him was mostly a short-term proposition. They saw him, according to a team source, as a solid veteran who was smart and talented enough to get them through a short stretch if Dart went down. Their faith gets shakier when it’s a long-term proposition they were hoping to avoid, especially since Winston last started more than seven games in a season seven years ago.

With Jaxson Dart out, what’s next for Giants, Jameis Winston? | ESPN.com

How does the offense adjust under Winston? It’s going to look different. Winston doesn’t have the same running ability as Dart. That much was obvious against the Rams when Winston rushed for 1 yard in three-plus quarters. That will hurt their traditional running game, too, since they designed an offense around Dart’s athletic skill set.

The Jameis experience comes with fire quotes, plenty of chuckles and a wide range of play. It’s not uncommon to see a spectacular tight-window throw down the field followed by a pass that sails 15 yards over a receiver’s head. It will be on this veteran offensive coaching staff, led by coordinator Matt Nagy, to limit the latter. Don’t ask Winston to do too much. Rely on the physical running game to downplay his proclivity for mistakes and interceptions.

Exploring quarterback options for Giants to add following Jaxson Dart’s season-ending injury | SNY.tv

Among the names being mentioned include FA Jimmy Garoppolo, Bengals Josh Johnson, recently signed by the Jets Will Levis, Vikings J.J. McCarthy, and last year’s starter Russell Wilson.

ESPN analysts: Giants should ‘kick the tires’ on this young QB | NJ.com

“Joe Milton is a young quarterback that can run,” ESPN’s Jordan Rodgers, a former college QB, said Wednesday on Get Up. “Not that he’s a dynamic runner, but he can do what Dart did in the zone read. He did it in college. He’s a big, physical guy, he could push the ball downfield. I think you kick the tires on Joe Milton, see if he can be traded for a late-round draft pick just so the identity of your offense doesn’t have to completely change with Jameis Winston and you could maybe still compete.”

2026 NFL offensive line rankings | PFF

21. New York Giants (up 1). The Giants struggled more up front in Week 2 than Week 1, with left tackle Andrew Thomas the only starter to muster a PFF grade above 70.0. Rookie right guard Francis Mauigoa had flashes in the run game, receiving a positive grade on 14.3% of run-blocking snaps compared with a 9.5% negatively graded play rate, but he concluded with just an 84.2% PFF pass-block win rate.

Resetting expectations for these six NFL teams with injured quarterbacks | CBSSports.com

New expectations: Vie for another early draft pick. There is no sugar coating the Giants’ outlook without Dart. What had all the makings of a (finally) exciting year is already down the tubes. That history suggests that so long as Winston is the man under center, New York will stand among the worst teams in the NFL. The silver lining is that the Giants should be able to add more premium young talent to their enticing core in the 2027 draft, but this was supposed to be a season in which that group elevated them out of the early draft pick range and into playoff contention.

item.title: What happened to Tua Tagovailoa? Falcons QB injury update as Michael Penix Jr. starts
item.description: Tua Tagovailoa initially topped the Falcons' QB depth chart to begin the 2026 season, but he never made a start for the team. Here's why.
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Falcons had one of the few open quarterback competitions ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Veteran free-agent signing Tua Tagovailoa was expected to battle with 2024 first-round pick Michael Penix Jr. for the right to start in Week 1.

That competition never materialized. Penix missed the entire preseason while recovering from a torn ACL he suffered during the 2025 season, which effectively handed Tagovailoa the starting job by default.

Even despite that, Tagovailoa has yet to make his regular-season debut for the Falcons. The 28-year-old suffered an injury in the lead-up to Week 1 and hasn't yet returned to the field.

Now, with Penix healthy and getting the nod in Week 3, many are wondering whether Tagovailoa will get a chance to try to resurrect his NFL career with the Falcons.

Here's what to know about Tagovailoa's status and his standing in the Falcons' quarterback room.

What happened to Tua Tagovailoa?

Tagovailoa is dealing with an oblique injury he suffered in practice on Thursday, Sept. 10.

Tagovailoa was injured during a passing drill. He attempted a pass but then immediately hunched over in pain, reaching for his back and crumpling to the ground. He received medical attention on the field and did not return to practice, standing off to the side while watching the session.

The Falcons listed Tagovailoa as "limited" on the team's practice report, casting doubt on his availability for Week 1. He was eventually ruled out for the contest and also did not play in Week 2 because of the injury.

Tua Tagovailoa injury update

The good news for Tagovailoa? He is evidently getting close to making his Falcons debut.

Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski wouldn't commit to Tagovailoa being active for the team's "Thursday Night Football" clash with the Green Bay Packers, but he also indicated the 28-year-old was generating positive momentum.

"We’ll see," Stefanski told reporters when asked about Tagovailoa's status. "But he’s trending in the right direction."

Later that day, the Falcons released their final injury report for the week. Tagovailoa was listed without an injury status, meaning he should be available to play Thursday, though that doesn't necessarily guarantee he will be active.

But even with his return arriving, Tagovailoa appears to have missed his window to emerge as the Falcons' starter.

Falcons QB depth chart

Penix is getting the nod after being a full participant in practice in the early stages of the 2026 NFL season.

Below is a full look at the Falcons' depth chart ahead of their "Thursday Night Football" game against the Packers:

  1. Michael Penix Jr.
  2. Tua Tagovailoa
  3. Cooper Rush
  4. Jack Strand

Rush started each of the Falcons' first two games with Penix and Tagovailoa hurt. The veteran struggled, completing 56.4% of his passes for 229 yards, one touchdown and four interceptions.

Strand, an undrafted rookie from Minnesota State – Moorhead, served as Rush's backup. He relieved his elder counterpart in the team's Week 2 blowout loss to the Carolina Panthers, completing 8 of 15 passes for 59 yards and an interception.

It isn't clear whether Rush or Strand will be designated the Falcons' emergency, third-string quarterback if Tagovailoa plays Thursday's game.

Tua Tagovailoa contract

The Falcons did not have to invest heavily to land Tagovailoa in free agency. Atlanta inked him to a one-year contract worth a veteran minimum of $1.215 million, as the former Dolphins starter was already on the hook to make $54 million from his former team.

Any money Atlanta paid Tagovailoa would have simply offset what Miami owed him. As such, it behooved Tagovailoa to take the veteran minimum deal, granting the Falcons maximum flexibility while ensuring the Dolphins remain on the hook for roughly $52.785 million of his overall earnings for 2026.

Tagovailoa will be a free agent after the 2026 NFL season.
